root_cause.text: Bitfield read-modify-write (RMW) operations on the `claimed` flag shared a memory word with retune control flags, causing concurrent writes from different contexts to corrupt adjacent bitfield members through unprotected RMW cycles.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `claimed`, `can_retune`, `retune_now`, and `retune_paused` from a shared bitfield word (where they were defined as `unsigned int` with `:1` bit widths) to individual `bool` members. The CVE description explicitly states: "Writes to claimed in __mmc_claim_host() or retune_now in mmc_mq_queue_rq() can overwrite other bits when concurrent updates happen in other contexts." This occurs because bitfield RMW operations are not atomic—a CPU must read the entire word, modify the target bit, and write the word back, during which concurrent modifications to other bits in the same word can be lost. By converting these flags to separate `bool` members, each flag gets its own memory location, eliminating the shared-word coupling and the RMW race condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restructure mmc_host struct layout by extracting `claimed` as a full bool and removing unused retune-related bitfields to optimize memory alignment and padding.
intent_record.what: Moved the `claimed` field from a 1-bit bitfield to a full `bool` type positioned before the bitfield group, and removed five bitfields (`can_retune`, `retune_now`, `retune_paused`) from the bitfield group, leaving only `use_spi_crc`, `doing_init_tune`, `doing_retune`, `retune_crc_disable`, `can_dma_map_merge`, and `vqmmc_enabled`.
intent_record.how: This change increases memory usage for the `claimed` field (from 1 bit to 8 bytes on 64-bit systems) but may improve cache locality and reduce padding overhead by consolidating the bitfield group. The removed bitfields (`can_retune`, `retune_now`, `retune_paused`) are no longer part of the `mmc_host` structure, eliminating their storage and any code that depends on them must be updated or removed elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce three new boolean fields to the mmc_host structure to provide more granular re-tuning state management alongside existing re-tuning controls.
intent_record.what: Added three new boolean fields (can_retune, retune_now, retune_paused) to the mmc_host structure, positioned before the existing need_retune field. These fields use bool type instead of int, and include descriptive comments explaining their purposes.
intent_record.how: This change expands the re-tuning state machine for MMC hosts by introducing three new flags that provide finer-grained control over re-tuning behavior: can_retune tracks whether re-tuning is supported, retune_now signals an immediate re-tuning request, and retune_paused allows temporary suspension of re-tuning. These complement the existing need_retune and hold_retune fields, enabling more sophisticated re-tuning logic at runtime.
